title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for T1DM and polyneuropathy.

HPI
Pt is an 83y female presenting for routine management of type 1 diabetes mellitus. Pt reports stable glucose levels and continues to use insulin for glycemic control. She complains of persistent tingling and numbness in bilateral feet, consistent with her known polyneuropathy. Denies acute changes in sensation or new-onset ulcers.

Medication List
Insulin glargine (long-acting)
Insulin lispro (rapid-acting) PRN

Exam
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Vitals: BP 128/78, HR 72, RR 16, Temp 98.6F, SpO2 97% on RA.
Physical: Skin intact, no visible ulcers on feet. Decreased sensation to monofilament testing in bilateral toes. No edema.
Neuro: Gait steady, RRR, CTAB.

Assessment
1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus.
2. Polyneuropathy.

Plan
1. Continue current insulin regimen.
2. Monitor blood glucose logs.
3. Foot care education provided; pt to inspect feet daily.
4. F/u in 3 months.

Electronically signed
P. O'Brien, PA-C
05/14/2026
explanations: Polyneuropathy is listed under 'with' for diabetes: E10.42.
Do not assign Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes; insulin use is inherent.

distractors.why: Coding separately misses the presumed link.
Z79.4 is not assigned for type 1 diabetes.
